newsitem.title: UK: ENGLAND SOCCER STAR CRITICISED IN PARLIAMENT.
newsitem.headline: ENGLAND SOCCER STAR CRITICISED IN PARLIAMENT.

text.p: English footballer Paul Gascoigne, who confessed he "deeply regretted what happened" after he was alleged to have beaten his wife, was criticised in parliament on Tuesday for setting a bad example for his adoring fans.

"He is not only getting away with serious assault, but he is being seen to get away with it. And worse, he is almost being rewarded into the bargain," said Roseanna Cunningham, of the Scottish National Party.
"He has said sorry. He has given a touching explanation about his bad temper and he knows he is in the wrong," she said of the star midfielder for Rangers of Glasgow.
"But where is the lesson for all the thousands of youngsters who lionise people such as him?" she asked during a House of Commons debate on crime and punishment.

Gascoigne, who is preparing for England's World Cup qualifier in the former Soviet republic of Georgia on Saturday, told a new conference on Monday he was seeking help for his problems through counselling.
His inclusion on the England squad following newspaper allegations that he beat his wife Sheryl caused a storm of protest, particularly from women's groups.

"I don't blame the women's groups for wanting me kicked out of the squad," Gascoigne admitted. "They have their right to say that and in the last week or so leading up to the announcement I didn't think I was going to be in the squad."
